scope: Third-party firmware (Kwrt and similar) computer-side dependency download: when the router cannot reach its own package source, the PC downloads the missing packages and transfers them for a native install. The device's real configured opkg feeds are tried first, and the OpenWrt official mirror is kept as a fallback. Dependency backup originals and signal dependencies follow the same policy.
root_cause: Two Kwrt-specific guards blocked the approved three-route flow. In dependency_manager._install_online and signal_manager.install_dependencies a network failure was re-raised unchanged for Kwrt instead of converting to offline_retry, so install_with_sources never reached route 3/3 (computer download). In addition the computer download for any non-OpenWrt device resolved packages only from the official OpenWrt mirrors (downloads.openwrt.org / archive.openwrt.org), never from the device's own source (for the logged device, https://dl.openwrt.ai).
behavior: Dependency install and signal dependency install now convert a verified network/source failure to offline_retry for every firmware, so the three-route flow reaches the computer download for Kwrt as documented (local -> router online -> computer download).

For third-party firmware (normalize_profile compatibility_trial == "kwrt", i.e. any distribution other than OpenWrt), the computer download now uses download_third_party_packages: it first reads the device's own configured opkg feeds and downloads the missing closure from those exact HTTPS URLs; if that fails (no readable feed, package not found, or download/checksum failure) it falls back to the firmware's official OpenWrt branch directories through download_profile_packages.
A cancellation never triggers the official fallback; the router command error is surfaced instead.
Official OpenWrt install/offline behavior is unchanged: OpenWrt stable/RC/SNAPSHOT still uses the official mirror/branch directories only.
Both download sources share one implementation for candidate protection, size limits, sha256 verification and the local cache (_verify_and_store); no cache, verification or size rule was relaxed.

Source validation is unchanged: only https feeds without credentials/query/fragment are accepted; signatures, hashes, installed-version comparison and the native opkg no-op simulation still apply; no new force option and no firmware source edit.
Dependency backup already routes non-OpenWrt firmware to fetch_configured_original, which downloads from the device's configured feeds on the PC; a Kwrt regression now pins that dispatch.

kwrt_official_source_review.method: Read the official Kwrt build repository (kiddin9/Kwrt) README, settings.ini and build workflow, and queried the author's GitHub repositories, branches, tags and releases through the GitHub API.
findings: kiddin9/Kwrt README states the only self-built package repository is dl.openwrt.ai ('自建在线插件仓库 dl.openwrt.ai').
The build workflow uploads compiled firmware/repository output only to the dl.openwrt.ai server (TARGET: /www/wwwroot/dl.openwrt.ai/releases/tmp/); no second distribution domain is configured.
kiddin9/Kwrt has no GitHub releases and no tags at review time.

kiddin9/packages-compile publishes some compiled .ipk files to GitHub releases per architecture; kiddin9/op-packages carries per-plugin .ipk in git; kiddin9/bin holds only sing-box/xray binaries. None of these provide an opkg Packages index or signatures and none covers the base/target feed, so none is a drop-in opkg source.

The Kwrt build is based on upstream OpenWrt (settings.ini REPO_URL=https://github.com/openwrt/openwrt, branch openwrt-25.12), so the official OpenWrt fallback is structurally related but the kernel build and package versions differ; candidate protection and the native simulation remain the safety net.

official_verification.method: Attempted to read the logged device's real feed during the change and reviewed the official Kwrt build repository; the official OpenWrt mirror layout was already documented and is unchanged.
findings: dl.openwrt.ai and openwrt.ai returned Cloudflare HTTP 523 (origin unreachable) for the site root and for /releases/25.12/packages/aarch64_cortex-a53/base/Packages.gz at change time, so the real Kwrt index/signature layout could not be fetched for this record.

Because the device's own configured feeds are read first, the PC fetches exactly the URLs the router uses, including the Kwrt target path that carries the kernel build (targets/<target>/<kernel>/Packages.gz); this avoids guessing a mirror layout.
Third-party firmware is outside the official OpenWrt compatibility scope; this change does not relax any official offline bundle identity check.

new_tests: tests/test_configured_package_feed.py: 14 tests covering PC download from the device's real source, https/credential rejection, one dead feed not hiding a usable feed, core-package protection before any package download, honest all-sources-unreadable error, cancel before download, Kwrt online failure reaching offline_retry, Kwrt offline preferring the device source, OpenWrt offline keeping the official mirror, Kwrt signal dependency failure reaching offline_retry, device-source success not touching the official mirror, device-source failure falling back to the official mirror, cancellation not falling back, and Kwrt backup original dispatch to the PC configured download.
coverage: Kwrt is not special-cased out of the computer download route anymore
the computer downloads from the device's configured https feeds first and only falls back to the official OpenWrt mirror when that fails
candidate protection and hash checks are shared and still reject core packages and existing packages
OpenWrt still uses the official mirror path only
tests.syntax_and_utf8_check: passed (py_compile on edited modules and the new test; Chinese literals written only through the file tool)

limitations: No real-router run: dl.openwrt.ai was returning HTTP 523 during the change, so the Kwrt feed could not be exercised end to end from the PC either.
No Debian 12 desktop run; the new code is pure Python and reuses the existing transport, so no platform branch was added.

The logged device's failure was a source-level network failure (wget returned 4); this change makes the PC route reachable and adds an official fallback, but a device whose real source is itself unreachable depends on the fallback matching the firmware.
Feature is a user-authorized exception for third-party firmware; it is not an official OpenWrt compatibility claim and does not extend official offline package coverage.
